RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — CPT 29806, Shoulder Labral/Instability Repair
Reference Number: POC-5BC96481D7-41351

To the Appeals Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29806 (arthroscopic shoulder capsulorrhaphy/labral repair), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-18. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I respectfully disagree and ask that this decision be reversed based on the clinical record summarized below and the plan's own applicable clinical criteria.

**Governing criteria applied to this request**

My understanding, based on Sunflower Health Plan's own published provider materials, is that non-emergent shoulder surgery — including "Shoulder Labral Repair" — is reviewed for medical necessity under Evolent's clinical guideline, currently titled "Evolent Clinical Guideline 1770 for Shoulder Arthroscopy" (Guideline Number: Evolent_CG_1770), with a Last Revised Date of December 2025 and an Implementation Date of July 2026. I am requesting that the plan confirm this is the exact guideline and version applied to my request and provide the complete text of the "Anterior-Inferior Labral Tear (Bankart Lesion)" section, since I was not able to obtain the full current wording of that specific subsection despite multiple attempts to locate it. Everything I cite below that I could confirm verbatim from the guideline is quoted directly; everything else is described in my own words.

**1. General Requirements (quoted verbatim from Evolent_CG_1770)**

The guideline states that elective shoulder surgery "may be considered if the following general criteria are met":

"Clinical correlation of individual's subjective complaints with objective exam findings and/or imaging (when applicable)"
"Individual has limited function (age-appropriate activities of daily living (ADLs), occupational, or athletic)"
"Individual is medically stable and optimized for surgery, and any treatable comorbidities are adequately medically managed..."
"Individual does not have an active local or systemic infection"
"Individual does not have active, untreated drug dependency (including but not limited to narcotics, opioids, muscle relaxants) unless engaged in a treatment program"

My record satisfies each of these:

- Clinical correlation: My 14 months of recurrent instability with apprehension, three anterior dislocations (the last requiring emergency-department reduction), and positive apprehension, relocation, and load-and-shift testing on exam are directly corroborated by the 2026-06-20 MR arthrogram showing an anteroinferior labral (Bankart) tear with a small Hill-Sachs lesion and glenoid bone loss under 10%.
- Limited function: I avoid overhead reaching and cannot return to work duties that require lifting.
- Medical stability: BMI is 29, I am a non-smoker, and I have no other untreated comorbidity.
- No active infection is present.
- No untreated substance dependency is present.

The guideline also states, under its Special Note: "In order for surgeries to be considered medically necessary there must be clear medical records that demonstrate a clear surgical plan that matches the request for surgery." Dr. Duval's operative plan for arthroscopic Bankart repair (CPT 29806) matches the diagnosis of anteroinferior labral tear with recurrent instability documented throughout the chart.

**2. The imaging findings do support — rather than contradict — medical necessity**

The stated basis for denial was that imaging does not support medical necessity. The 2026-06-20 MR arthrogram documents exactly the pathology relevant to this procedure: an anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion), a small Hill-Sachs lesion, and glenoid bone loss under 10%, with an intact rotator cuff. I am not aware of any language in the plan's guideline that requires findings beyond a demonstrated labral tear correlated with clinical instability, and I ask the plan to identify the specific imaging criterion it believes was not met, quoting the exact guideline language, so that I can respond directly.

**3. Bankart/labral-repair-specific criteria**

The most recent version of this guideline's criteria for labral repair that I was able to obtain in full is from Evolent's (formerly National Imaging Associates') "Shoulder Arthroscopy Clinical Tip Sheet," which summarized the prior version of this same guideline (then numbered Evolent_CG-318). I am citing it only as the best available description of the plan's approach to Bankart repair, not as confirmed current wording of Evolent_CG_1770, and I am asking the plan to confirm whether the current criteria differ. That tip sheet stated that Bankart repair for a recurrent labral tear "may be necessary when ALL the following criteria are met":

"Recurrent instability (subluxation or dislocation)"
"Evidence of a labral tear with or without bony Bankart fracture of the glenoid upon imaging"
"Range of motion is not limited by stiffness upon physical exam"
"Clinical exam findings demonstrate positive apprehension test, positive relocation test, positive labral grind test, or objective laxity with pain"

My record meets each of these as described:

- Recurrent instability: Three anterior dislocations since symptom onset, the most recent reduced in the emergency department.
- Imaging evidence of labral tear: The 2026-06-20 MR arthrogram confirms an anteroinferior (Bankart) labral tear.
- Range of motion: Examination documented full strength with no restriction from stiffness.
- Positive exam findings: Positive apprehension test, positive relocation test, and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift testing (objective laxity), all documented on exam.

That same tip sheet further indicated that for Bankart tears, "[n]on-operative treatment not required if the following criteria are met" — i.e., a trial of conservative care is not a prerequisite for this specific diagnosis. Nonetheless, I completed 16 weeks (2026-03-16 to 2026-07-06, 18 visits) of supervised physical therapy targeting rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening with activity modification, plus 4 months of NSAIDs during flares, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. An intra-articular injection was not pursued because it is not indicated for instability. This additional conservative-care record further supports, rather than undermines, medical necessity.

**Requested action**

Based on the above, I ask that Sunflower Health Plan/Evolent reverse the denial of CPT 29806 and approve the requested arthroscopic Bankart repair. If any specific element of the applicable guideline is still considered unmet, I request that the plan identify the exact criterion and quote the exact guideline language relied upon, along with a complete copy of the "Anterior-Inferior Labral Tear (Bankart Lesion)" section of Evolent_CG_1770 as currently in effect, so that the treating surgeon and I may respond to it directly.

Enclosed / available upon request:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-16 to 2026-07-06, 18 visits)
- MR arthrogram report dated 2026-06-20
- Office/exam notes documenting recurrent dislocation history, apprehension/relocation/load-and-shift findings, and functional limitations
- Emergency department record of most recent dislocation/reduction
- Surgeon's (Dr. Duval, MD) operative plan and letter of medical necessity

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide written notice of the outcome. I understand this appeal is timely, as it is being submitted within 180 days of the 2026-08-18 notice (by 2027-02-14).

Sincerely,

Riley Hayes
